pr.title: Do not unify dereferences of shared borrows in GVN
pr.description:
Repost of https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/132461, the last commit applies my suggestions.

Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/130853
pr.author: RalfJung

analysis.summary: GVN historically treated dereferences of shared references to `Freeze` pointees as reusable values, allowing a load before an opaque call to be substituted for a later load after that call. The PR marks this as unsound (issue #130853), disables it unless `-Zunsound-mir-opts` is enabled, and updates GVN/MIR and coverage expectations.
analysis.originalLogic: In `VnState` projection handling for `ProjectionElem::Deref`, GVN checked that the place type was a shared reference (`Some(Mutability::Not) = ty.ref_mutability()`), that a builtin pointee existed, and that `pointee_ty.is_freeze(self.tcx, self.typing_env())`; if so, it canonicalized the dereference as a reusable value expression. That allowed repeated shared-borrow dereferences, including nested `&&u8` reads, to be unified across intervening opaque calls.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: GVN reused/unified a dereference of a shared borrow to a `Freeze` pointee as if the loaded value were invariant over an opaque side effect. In the regression shape `let y = **x; unsafe { unknown() }; **x == y`, the old behavior could propagate the first `**x` load into the comparison after `unknown()`; old test expectations explicitly stated “We can substitute through an immutable reference too” and “We can reuse dereferences of `&Freeze`.” The corrected GVN output keeps the second load and ends with `_0 = Eq(move _4, copy _2)` rather than proving the result constant true.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR functions containing shared-reference dereferences, especially nested shared references such as `&&u8` or dereferences of `&Freeze` pointees, where a value is read before and after an opaque/inline-never call.
analysis.trigger: A dereference through a shared reference whose pointee is `Freeze` is followed by an opaque call and another dereference/read of the same place, under GVN without the `unsound_mir_opts` guard.
preconditions: GVN processes a `ProjectionElem::Deref` on a place whose type is a shared reference (`Mutability::Not`).
The old code lacks the `self.tcx.sess.opts.unstable_opts.unsound_mir_opts` guard.
An observable side effect such as an opaque or inline-never call occurs between two reads, so reusing the earlier read changes behavior under valid unsafe aliasing.
pitfalls: Do not conflate `T: Freeze` with the stability of the storage holding a shared reference; the shared reference itself may be mutated through unsafe aliasing, which is why issue #130853 marks this optimization unsound.
Checking only for a shared reference or only for `Freeze` is insufficient; the old reuse condition combined both and is now gated by `unsound_mir_opts`.
Nested dereferences and reborrows are distinct cases; this fix disables shared-borrow dereference unification, not all dereferences of mutable references or raw pointers.
Coverage `.cov-map` and PreCodegen test changes are consequences of no longer performing the optimization, not independent GVN correctness preconditions.
A retained test name or old comment/expectation does not prove a replacement pass is wrong; compare the actual value assignments in the decoded MIR revisions.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a MIR-opt regression test, run for both panic strategies, using `fn src(x: &&u8)` with `let y = **x;`, then `unsafe { unknown() };`, then `**x == y`, where `unknown` is `#[inline(never)]`. Assert after GVN that the second load is retained and the comparison is `_0 = Eq({{.*}}, {{.*}})`, with `CHECK-NOT: _0 = const true;`. Also retain/update focused GVN expectations such as the `&Freeze` case and the `borrowed<T: Copy + Freeze>` case, and exercise the old rule only behind `-Zunsound-mir-opts`.
evidence: -    // We can substitute through an immutable reference too.
+    // We cannot substitute through an immutable reference.
